tagline: Self-hosted social media scheduler for 13 networks with calendar, approvals, REST API and an MCP server.
description: TryPost is a social media scheduler built with Laravel and Vue. A composer writes a post once and adapts it per network, with a live preview. Posts go onto a calendar or into per-channel queues that fill the next free slot. Members can send posts for approval, and admins approve or reject them. Workspaces keep brands or clients apart, which suits agencies. The README lists Instagram, TikTok, LinkedIn, X, YouTube, Facebook, Threads, Bluesky, Pinterest, Mastodon, Google Business, Telegram and Discord, each published through the network's official API. A REST API and an MCP server with more than 80 tools let scripts or AI assistants create posts and read analytics. Webhooks report when posts are published or fail. The licence is AGPL-3.0, and the README says the self-hosted version has every feature of the paid cloud, with no locked tiers. A deployment guide is in the repository and the supported route is Docker. Publishing to each network needs developer access to its API, so expect to register apps on the platforms you use. The project started in January 2026, so it is young compared with Hootsuite.
strengths: Publishes to 13 networks through their official APIs, with no reminder-only fallback
Per-channel queues and a drag-to-reschedule calendar
Approval flow and separate workspaces for agencies handling many brands
REST API, webhooks and an MCP server with 80+ tools
Self-hosted edition has all features of the cloud edition, with no paid tiers
limits: A young project: the repository was created in 2026, so expect a changing feature set
Each network's API access, keys and review rules are yours to set up when self-hosting
AGPL-3.0 requires publishing your changes if you run a modified version as a network service
The README describes no inbox, social listening or ad management
Stack of PHP, Laravel and Vue means you need that skill set to debug or extend it
bestFor: A small agency or in-house team that schedules posts for several brands and wants to run the tool on its own server.
